title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
technique: Hopper-specific warp-specialized producer/consumer pipelining, ping-pong softmax/GEMM overlap, FP8 attention with block quantization and incoherent processing

optimized_metrics.evidence: FlashAttention-2 nonetheless achieves poor utilization on newer GPUs relative to optimized matrix-multiplication (GEMM) kernels, such as 35% vs. 80-90% on the Hopper H100 GPU.
We develop three main techniques to speed up attention on Hopper GPUs
We use the techniques of block quantization and incoherent processing to mitigate the loss of accuracy that results from moving to FP8 precision.

headline_claim.text: FlashAttention-3, achieves speedup on H100 GPUs by 1.5-2.0× with FP16 reaching up to 740 TFLOPs/s (75% utilization), and with FP8 reaching close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We benchmark the speed on an H100 80GB SXM5 (700W). ... We repeat the benchmarks 100 times and take the average timing.
metric_definitions.notes: Utilization = achieved attention TFLOPs/s over H100 FP16 theoretical max (≈989 TFLOPs/s dense); the paper gives no separate formal definition beyond the FLOPs formula, same as FA2 (4*seqlen^2*d*heads, halved for causal)

load_regime: sequence-length sweep with fixed total tokens (16k) kernel microbenchmark
tradeoff_acknowledged: FP8 raises numerical error (baseline FP8 RMSE 2.4e-2) vs FP16 (1.9e-4); mitigated by block quantization + incoherent processing to 9.1e-3.
workloads: synthetic Q/K/V; head dim 64/128/256; causal and non-causal
extractor_notes: Kernel-level only; design targets achieved TFLOPs/s (UTIL) and kernel runtime, with numerical error as accuracy constraint. No end-to-end training or serving results; paper lists 'optimizing for LLM inference' as future work. No serving metric (TTFT/TPOT/throughput) appears.
